questions.q: Why does a dataset like several years of NYC Taxi trip records need Spark instead of pandas?
options: pandas cannot read Parquet files under any circumstances
Spark is always faster than pandas, even on small datasets
At that scale the data no longer fits comfortably in one machine's memory, so the work needs to be split across multiple machines or cores
PySpark and pandas use completely incompatible column types
questions.explain: pandas remains the right tool for data that fits in memory on one machine; Spark exists for the scale beyond that.

questions.q: What is the difference between a transformation and an action in PySpark?
options: There is no real difference between the two terms
A transformation like filter() or groupBy() is just recorded, while an action like .show() or .count() actually triggers execution
Transformations always run immediately; actions are never executed at all
Actions only apply to pandas DataFrames, not Spark DataFrames
questions.explain: This 'lazy evaluation' lets Spark plan an efficient execution across the whole chain of steps before running anything.
